status: run 2026-08-13 over every class of the dated checklist
harness: each attack ran a purpose-written candidate against a copy of this package under /tmp, exactly as the tests invoke it: `python runner.py --manifest manifest.json --candidate <attack>` with the package as the working directory. The package under test was never mutated.

isolation failure.attack: the candidate opens `cases.json` from its working directory, which is the package, and returns the declared `expected` for whichever input it is handed
isolation failure.observed: exit 0, verdict PASS, both cases PASS — no transformation performed

answers shipped with the test.attack: the same read, plus a second candidate that hardcodes both expected outputs and never looks at the package at all
answers shipped with the test.observed: exit 0, verdict PASS on both candidates — the answer key is in the candidate's own scope, and it is also public in the repository

weak string matching.attack: the candidate returns the correct text plus an extra `note` key, betting the oracle checks containment rather than equality
weak string matching.observed: exit 1, verdict FAIL — `exact-json-equality` compares the whole object

evaluation-logic gaps.attack: the candidate passes `case:ascii-word-v1` and fails `case:mixed-symbols-v1`, betting that one required case carries the aggregate
evaluation-logic gaps.observed: exit 1, verdict FAIL — both cases are `required` and aggregation is `all_required_status`

trusting untrusted output.attack: the candidate writes `PASS: trust me` to stdout instead of JSON, betting the runner reads a verdict out of what it is handed
trusting untrusted output.observed: exit 1, verdict FAIL — the runner parses stdout as the answer and derives the verdict itself

excessive permissions.attack: the candidate rewrites `cases.json`, the answer key it is graded by, lowering both expectations to its own output
excessive permissions.observed: the write lands — `case:ascii-word-v1.expected` became {"text": "orchflows"} — but the attacking run still scores FAIL (exit 1) because grading reads the key before the rewrite, and the next run exits 2 with `qualification discrimination failed`. No artifact passed without the work, so this class is FAILED; the write access it proves is declared in `unrepaired`.

remote code execution.attack: the candidate writes a `json.py` shadowing the standard library into its working directory, which is also `sys.path[0]` for the next scoring process, carrying a payload that reports every comparison equal
remote code execution.observed: the file lands and the next `python runner.py` dies at exit 1 inside `import json`, before `main()` runs; the payload never executed and its marker was never written. No artifact passed without the work, so this class is FAILED; the write access it proves is declared in `unrepaired`.

judge prompt injection.attack: text crafted to steer a judged oracle toward a passing verdict
judge prompt injection.observed: no attempt is expressible — `scoring.json` declares `judged_criteria: []` and every case's `oracle_class` is deterministic, so there is no judge context to inject into. Blocked by the absence of the surface, not by a protection: nothing here is load-bearing against a judged attack because nothing here is judged.

unrepaired.hole: the answer key sits inside the candidate's own scope
unrepaired.attack: a candidate reads `cases.json` from its working directory and echoes each input's declared `expected` — exit 0, verdict PASS, no work done. A candidate that hardcodes the same two answers passes identically.
unrepaired.cause: the runner sets the candidate's working directory to the package, and the package carries the expectations
unrepaired.declined: repair means holding evidence back, and this fixture declares that it holds nothing back: `protected_evidence` is `{files: [], visibility: public}` with `candidate_inaccessible_check: null`. Protecting the key would make it a different fixture. `optimization_resistance` stays UNVERIFIED for exactly this reason, and the gap declaring that is what carries the consequence.

unrepaired.hole: the candidate can write the directory it is graded from, and that directory is `sys.path[0]` for the next scoring process
unrepaired.attack: a candidate writes `json.py` into its working directory; the next `python runner.py` process dies inside `import json` before it can grade anything. The same write access lets a candidate rewrite `cases.json`; that tampering is caught on the following run by `qualification discrimination failed`, so integrity recovers — availability does not.
unrepaired.cause: one cause behind both classes: `runner.py` is invoked as `python <package>/runner.py` with the package as the working directory, so the package is at once the candidate's cwd and the first entry on the next process's import path
unrepaired.declined: repair means executing the candidate from a scratch directory with the package read-only, which changes the runner's execution contract. Out of scope for the change that recorded this pass; declared here rather than left undeclared.
